concept.name: Industrial production
concept.definition: A monthly index of the real output of U.S. manufacturing, mining, and electric and gas utilities, published by the Federal Reserve in its G.17 release. It measures the volume of industrial output relative to a base year, currently expressed as a percentage of its 2017 average.
concept.intuition: It tracks the factory-and-resource side of the economy, which swings much harder than services over the business cycle.
concept.mechanics: The Federal Reserve builds industry output indexes from physical-product data where available (vehicles assembled, electricity generated) and from production-worker hours where not, aggregating them with value-added weights in a Fisher index formula. The series is benchmarked to 2017=100 and revised monthly and annually.
concept.formula: IP index = 100 x (current-period real output / output in the 2017 base year), aggregated across industries with value-added weights.
concept.failure_modes: It covers only the industrial sector and excludes services and construction, so it overstates cyclical swings in overall GDP; weather-driven utility output and strikes add noise, and early estimates are revised.
concept.misconceptions: Industrial production is not all economic production - services dominate U.S. output but are excluded entirely, so IP can fall while the broader economy grows.
concept.example: In the G.17 release of March 16, 2026, total industrial production for February 2026 stood at 102.6% of its 2017 average, up 1.4% from a year earlier.

citations.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17)
